To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have isolated and sequenced a cDNA clone for the human vimentins gene.
we have isolated and determined the complete cDNA sequence of the human Vimentin gene.
we have isolated and sequenced the complete coding part (1398 bp, 466 amino acids) of the human vimen- tin gene (1765 bp).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular biology of the human videntin gene, a major component of the intermediate filament system.
the identification and characterization of the human vimitin gene, which is the first member of a family of intermediate filament proteins.
the molecular mechanisms involved in the regulation of cell proliferation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vimentin cDNA sequence presented here is in complete agreement with the published sequence (2, 4) except for the 44 bp mentioned above.
the vimentin gene contains 1398 bp coding for a protein of 466 amino acids and that the 3' untranslated sequence is 322 bp long.
the human vimentins are encoded by a single gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human vimenti n gene is composed of 10 exons and 9 introns.
the human viment type intermediate filament protein is encoded by a single gene, and that the cDNA contains a complete coding region and a part of the 3' untranslated sequence.
we have isolated the longest cDNA for human Vimentin to date, covering the complete coding region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the human vimentins gene is transcribed into a 1.7 kb mRNA.
the cDNA sequence of the human gene coding for vimentin has been determined in full length.
the complete coding sequence for human vementin can be isolated by reverse transcription of total mRNA from SV40 transformed fibroblasts.
